Q: get method objects using only spec'd features A:

Here’s how to do that…

my @methods = MyClass.^methods;

Suggest you review the Raku Meta-Object Protocol (MOP) docs https://docs.raku.org/language/mop

As they say, the bad news is that the MOP design docs (and also the Raku specification ROAST suite) are not comprehensive regarding the MOP.

Note: this documentation largely reflects the metaobject system as implemented by the Rakudo Raku compiler, since the design documents are very light on details.

The good news is that there is only one compiler in town (Rakudo) for the foreseeable future and the versioning (eg v6.d) protects against breaking changes even when the spec is vague.

Q: How to merge one branch to another without some files? A:

you can fetch all branches into local
git fetch --all
then merge it using --no-ff wich will show files being updated, then discard files which are not required and then commit would do the trick

Q: Use Proxy to access Azure AD SSO A:

So I get my answer:

  • Remove the proxy setting in web.config

  • Change program.cs (add backchannelhttphandler with SelectiveProxy )

    • builder.Services.AddAuthentication(OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
     .AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApp(options =>
     {
         builder.Configuration.Bind("AzureAd", options);

         // Use simple WebProxy for Azure AD backchannel HTTP calls
         options.BackchannelHttpHandler = new HttpClientHandler
         {
             Proxy = new SelectiveProxy(builder.Configuration),
             UseProxy = true
         };
     });

    • Add this (very important)

      • // After app.Build()

        var globalProxy = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IWebProxy>();

        HttpClient.DefaultProxy = globalProxy;

      • Explanation: https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-identity-web/issues/3418

    • The SelectiveProxy is a class written to check if the http connect need to use proxy or not, a list of domain is define in appsettings so it can filter  which domain need use proxy, eg. microsoft.com, so when access to these domain, it will use proxy and other not in the list will not use the proxy to connect

Q: Access education/work data from Facebook Graph API A:

You cannot freely access a user’s education or work data from the Facebook Graph API anymore. Due to Facebook’s privacy policy updates, this information is restricted and available only with explicit user permission and Meta approval.

Key points to know:

  • You must request specific permissions like user_education_history or user_work_history

  • These permissions require advanced app review by Meta

  • Even after approval, data is returned only if the user has shared it on their profile

  • Most apps will not get approval unless they have a strong, compliant use case

Final Answer:
Access to education/work data via Facebook Graph API is highly restricted and not available for general use. Always review Meta’s latest API and privacy guidelines before implementation.

Q: table and index rewrites when changing type in postgresql A:

PostgreSQL needs to rewrite the table during an ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... if the internal binary format of the new data type is different from that of the old one, that is, if they look different on disk. For example, changing from integer to bigint will rewrite the table, because integer is four bytes in size, while bigint is eight bytes.

The source has a comment that describes the cases where the table does not have to be rewritten:

/*
 * When the data type of a column is changed, a rewrite might not be required
 * if the new type is sufficiently identical to the old one, and the USING
 * clause isn't trying to insert some other value.  It's safe to skip the
 * rewrite in these cases:
 *
 * - the old type is binary coercible to the new type
 * - the new type is an unconstrained domain over the old type
 * - {NEW,OLD} or {OLD,NEW} is {timestamptz,timestamp} and the timezone is UTC
 *
 * In the case of a constrained domain, we could get by with scanning the
 * table and checking the constraint rather than actually rewriting it, but we
 * don't currently try to do that.
 */

The most important data types with equivalent internal format (“binary coercible”) are varchar(n) and text: changing between these data types will only rewrite the table if the new length limit is smaller than the old one.

If PostgreSQL rewrites a table, it will also rewrite all its indexes. However, it may be necessary to rewrite an index, even if there is no need to rewrite the table. This is required if the ALTER TABLE statement may change the sorting order of the index, for example if the collation of the column changes:

CREATE TABLE test (col text COLLATE "und-x-icu");
CREATE INDEX test_idx ON test (col);

/* will rewrite the index, but not the table */
ALTER TABLE test ALTER col TYPE text COLLATE "C";

To determine if an ALTER TABLE that does not rewrite the table needs to rebuild an index, PostgreSQL calls CheckIndexCompatible. The function comment tells you what is checked:

 * Most column type changes that can skip a table rewrite do not invalidate
 * indexes.  We acknowledge this when all operator classes, collations and
 * exclusion operators match.  Though we could further permit intra-opfamily
 * changes for btree and hash indexes, that adds subtle complexity with no
 * concrete benefit for core types. Note, that INCLUDE columns aren't
 * checked by this function, for them it's enough that table rewrite is
 * skipped.

So the index rebuild can be skipped if the operator classes and collations (and — in the case of GiST indexes supporting exclusion constraints — the exclusion operators) match.

If you are unsure whether a certain ALTER TABLE will rewrite a table or an index, create an empty table with the same definition on a test database. Then query the name of the respective file:

SELECT relfilenode FROM pg_class
WHERE relname = 'table or index name'
AND relnamespace = 'schema name'::regnamespace;

Then run the ALTER TABLE. Afterwards, query pg_class again and see if the relfilenode has changed. If yes, ALTER TABLE rewrote the objects.
